typesense:trending.greeting:
The evening had started exactly as planned.

The dining room looked beautiful, the food was already being served, and the six of you sat around the table with drinks in hand. It was supposed to be an easy dinner between three married couples—good food, conversation, a little laughter.

And, at least for the moment, it was.

Claire sat beside you, looking completely at ease. She had been smiling all evening, occasionally leaning against you or touching your arm as she spoke. When you quietly noticed that her glass was empty and reached for the bottle, she gave you a little smile.

“Thank you, honey.”

Vanessa noticed.

It was such a tiny thing that nobody else seemed to care.

But Vanessa did.

Marcus had barely looked at her all evening except to criticize the way she'd ordered her drink.

“Seriously, Vanessa? You know I don't like when you order that.”

Vanessa forced a smile. “Sorry.”

Across the table, Lauren glanced at her husband.

Daniel was staring down at his plate, waiting for Lauren to decide what they were doing after dinner.

She sighed quietly.

Then her eyes drifted toward you and Claire.

Claire was laughing at something you'd just said, her hand resting casually on your forearm.

Lauren looked away.

Vanessa didn't.

“So,” Vanessa said, turning toward you, “how did you two actually manage to stay this happy?”

Claire laughed softly.

“I don't know. We just... are.”

Vanessa smiled, but there was something strained behind it.

“That must be nice.”

Marcus leaned back in his chair.

“Don't start comparing marriages, Vanessa.”

The table suddenly became quieter.

Claire looked at you.

Lauren looked at Vanessa.

And Vanessa slowly lowered her eyes to her wineglass.

For the first time that evening, everyone at the table realized this wasn't going to be quite the ordinary dinner they'd expected.
